A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EditRoom with the same authors, method and experimental framework. The text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 2–5, plus qualitative single-operation and multi-operation results in Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 reports revised quantitative comparisons and ablations, retains the qualitative editing results, and adds a denoising visualization in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o command planner, six editing operations, graph and layout diffusion stages, representations, losses and inference procedure are unchanged. The new denoising appendix illustrates the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use EditRoom-DB derived from 3D-FRONT and 3D-FUTURE, covering bedrooms, dining rooms, living rooms and the same six operations. Single-operation and compositional editing scenarios remain unchanged; the expanded test sample counts concern E3.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 and Figures 3–4 retain DiffuScene-N and SceneEditor-N as comparators. The conditioning and text-encoder alternatives also remain unchanged. Correcting DiffuScene-E to DiffuScene-N in the setup does not introduce a different baseline; Ma et al. is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 expand the reported test set from 1,500 to 7,800 samples: bedroom/dining/living counts change from 500/500/500 to 4,800/1,500/1,500. Operation counts become nearly balanced within each room, also changing the room weighting of pooled results. Training settings, metrics and the 24-view rendering protocol are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B and Figure 5 add a qualitative process case study showing intermediate denoising layouts for adding a wardrobe. The existing conditioning and text-encoder ablation questions remain unchanged; their revised numerical outcomes are covered under E6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The larger test set does not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 substantially replace the quantitative results. For example, EditRoom bedroom IOU changes from 0.7435 to 0.7342, while removal IOU changes from 0.5556 to 0.6399. These accompany a changed test set and are not same-setting performance changes. EditRoom remains best across the reported metrics. Figure 5 additionally reports intermediate denoising outcomes.

T1.justification: The scene-graph definitions, conditional formulation and losses in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. The collision-detection reasoning is retained in the relocated pipeline appendix. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: unified six-operation editing, an approximately 83k-pair dataset, superior comparative performance and compositional generalization without additional training. The new iterative-refinement wording elaborates existing editability without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: The introduction newly frames generated scenes as starting points for iterative user refinement. Appendix B explicitly links joint refinement of object properties during denoising to scene coherence. Existing interpretations of the ablations and limitations concerning LLM errors, collisions and unusual commands are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project website address in the abstract, providing a new access pointer. The Reproducibility Statement, implementation settings, supplied prompts and data-generation instructions are otherwise retained. The PDFs alone do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Ma et al. (2018) and contrasts earlier rule-based editing with diffusion-based diversity and generalization. It also revises the EchoScene discussion to emphasize target-scene-graph input and lack of textual instructions. The broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites related work, expands the introduction, adds a denoising appendix and changes the header to the ICLR 2025 publication designation. The dataset-pipeline appendix moves from B to C, while the overall narrative and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5 showing denoising stages. The existing prompt figures are retained as Figures 6–7, with accompanying appendix reflow. Main diagrams, qualitative comparison panels and table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The enlarged evaluation better represents previously sparse operations: for example, living-room rotation cases increase from 27 to 252, with more even operation counts throughout Table 1. The retained comparative conclusions, denoising illustration and added prior-work context provide bounded improvements in evidence and explanation. These gains are tempered by unchanged uncertainty reporting and a newly inconsistent Table 1 caption that still claims 500 test samples per room.
